ossified

OSS-uh-fyed · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ossified is become rigid and resistant to change.

Decades without reform had left the agency's procedures completely ossified.

Example

Once a flexible startup, the company's decision-making had become so ossified that even small changes required five layers of approval.

Ossified describes a system, structure, or set of rules that has become so fixed and unchanging over time that it can no longer adapt.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rigid: Rigid means fixed and unable to bend or change, whatever the reason -- a steel bar is rigid the day it is made. Ossified adds history: an ossified system has slowly hardened into rigidity over years of habit. Rigid names the state; ossified tells you it grew that way.

entrenched: An entrenched practice is firmly established and well defended, so people resist giving it up even when better options appear. An ossified one is worse off: it has hardened until it can no longer adapt at all, defenders or none. Entrenched things are guarded; ossified things cannot move.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

flexible: able to adapt and change easily

dynamic: constantly changing and active

Where it sits · how permanently set against change

outdated → ossified → fossilized

outdated vs. ossified: Something outdated is merely behind the times and could be brought current with one good update, a much milder condition than ossified, which has hardened against change itself.

fossilized vs. ossified: Something fossilized has hardened into permanent stone, an even more extreme rigidity than merely ossified.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — oss: bone (Latin (os, ossis))

suffix — -ify: to make, to turn into (Latin (-ificare))

suffix — -ed: having undergone the process of (Old English)

Put it together: oss ("bone") + -ify ("to make into") + -ed = turned into bone -- hardened and fixed.

Use the root in a new word: ossuary: Photography is not allowed inside the chapel's small medieval ossuary.

Word Choice

Ossified describes a system, structure, or process -- like a bureaucracy, a set of rules, or an institution -- that has hardened over time, distinct from "hidebound," which describes a person or group's stubborn attitude toward new ideas specifically.
